title: Can the first player always win?
hook: X moves first. Does that decide the game? Solve an endgame, then the empty board.

doesNotKnow: how a game can be solved by working back from the end

misconception: In noughts and crosses the first player, playing perfectly, wins.
objective: The learner can explain that a game is solved by scoring every ending and working upward, with each player picking the best result for themselves (O the worst for X), and that this gives a draw for tic-tac-toe.

claims.text: The bottom row is the same two rules, run by computer from the empty board. Corner, edge and centre each scored a draw, so X's best first move is a draw: perfect players always draw.

The other six first moves are mirror/rotation copies (not shown). claims.text: To solve a game, score every ending, then let each player pick the best result for themselves moving upward: O picks the worst result for X, X picks the best.

recall.question: X is to move. Scoring each of X's three moves by O's best reply gives: X wins, draw, O wins. What is the value of X's position with perfect play?
recall.why: X picks the move that is best for X, so the position takes the highest of the three scores. Each of those scores already assumed O's best reply.
